title: upgrade-attn-flashattnv2-rope-rotary-fused-kv-batching-scheduling
author: Priya Kumar
description: Background: This PR upgrades our attention execution path to the latest FlashAttentionV2 variant and introduces a set of fused rotary/rope ops plus integration work for KV-cache compatibility and scheduler heuristics to enable safer continuous batching. Motivation: reduce per-token latency and improve throughput on long-context workloads while avoiding regressions for smaller models and existing cached sessions. Summary of changes: 1) Upgrade FlashAttentionV2 kernels to upstream-v2.3 with our internal patches for max-seq handling and mixed-quant fast paths. 2) Implement fused rotary+rope operators (fused_rotary_rope.cu / fused_rotary_rope.cc) that combine rotary embeddings and rope conversion to reduce memory bandwidth and kernel launches. 3) Add KV-cache layout compatibility layer so new fused kernels can operate on both legacy and compact KV buffer formats without copying. 4) Scheduling changes: introduce a new continuous-batching heuristic that considers active KV-preserved sessions and max-latency SLOs; add backpressure thresholds to avoid large batch accumulation for latency-sensitive routes. 5) Runtime feature flags and fallbacks: when a fused kernel fails (cuda assert / unsupported shape) we gracefully fallback to the previous implementation and emit a metric. 6) Bench and test harness updates: end-to-end microbench and eval harness with synthetic long-context traces and real workload traces used by Redwood perf-lab. Checklist: - [x] Kernel implementation and unit tests - [x] Integration tests for KV cache compatibility - [x] Perf benchmarks + statistical analysis - [x] CI passes (with allowed flaky lint rerun) - [x] Docs: release notes and runtime feature flag docs Motivation/Context: We observed 12-18% p50 latency improvement on 8k context generation and 20-30% throughput improvements on multi-stream workloads in perf-lab when using fused rotary+rope on A100/RTX6000-class hardware with continuous batching enabled. Smaller models (<=2B) see modest gains (3-5%) and no regressions. Compatibility: To avoid invalidating in-use KV encodings, the compatibility layer detects buffer format at runtime and selects either the fused kernel or a thin-copy path. This keeps customer traffic safe during rollout. Commits (high-level): - feat(kernels): upgrade flashattnv2->v2.3 and add mixed-quant paths - feat(kernels): implement fused_rotary_rope kernels and operator - feat(runtime): KV-cache compatibility layer and detection hooks - feat(scheduler): continuous-batching heuristic + backpressure thresholds - test(perf): add long-context synthetic traces and bench harness - ci: adjust GPU job matrix for new kernels Tests & CI: Initial CI run had a failing lint check and one flaky unit test in attention UTs; after fixes CI passed on the final run. GPU integration tests were run on perf-canary infra and showed green on A100 and RTX6000 sims. Final CI status: pass. Files changed (high level): "libruntime/attention/flashattnv2_kernels.cu","libruntime/attention/fused_rotary_rope.cu","libruntime/attention/fused_rotary_rope.h","libruntime/kv/kv_compat_layer.cc","libruntime/scheduler/continuous_batching.cc","libruntime/scheduler/continuous_batching.h","tests/attention/attn_kernel_tests.cc","perf/benchmarks/long_context_bench.cc","docs/release_notes/2026-03-01-attn-kernel-upgrade.md","examples/bench/run_long_context.sh" Files changed count: 12 Additions: 1342 Deletions: 412 Reviewers: [Alex Chen, Mateo Rivera, Sofia Patel, James O'Neill] Review summary: - Alex Chen: requested a small API rename for clarity on the KV detection hook; asked for a regression test for shard boundary conditions. Response: renamed and added tests. - Mateo Rivera: flagged potential OOM case for continuous batching with many active sessions; requested a backpressure threshold and metric. Response: added config knob with sane default and metric emission. - Sofia Patel: asked for detailed bench artifacts and reproducibility notes; we uploaded perf-lab traces and reproduced results across two GPUs. - James O'Neill: verified kernel fallback path and approved after CI passed. Conversation highlights: reviewer comments, author replies and follow-ups are included as flattened review_comments below. Performance summary: - Long-context (8k) p50 latency: -15% to -18% across A100/RTX6000 - Throughput (multi-stream): +20-30% in continuous batching mode - Small models p50: -3% to -5% No customer-facing breaking changes. Release notes: "Upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 v2.3 with fused rotary+rope ops; improves long-context latency and throughput. Adds runtime feature flag 'enable_fused_rotary_rope' and a compatibility layer for KV buffers. Rollout: gradual by region with automatic fallback." Rollout plan: staged rollout using canary tag in Dedicated and Hosted: start with internal canary traffic -> perf-canary -> 10% of production -> 50% -> 100%. Monitoring: new metrics added: attn.fused_kernel_fallback_count, scheduler.continuous_batch_backpressure_count, attn.fused_kernel_latency_p50/p90. Linked work items: ENG-3421, ENG-3589 Linked support tickets: SUP-1182 (customer reported regen slowdown which this PR addresses) Linked PRs: references to prior kernel upgrade PRs pr-613579 and pr-589001 for history. Merge outcome: merged via squash-and-merge after approvals and green CI. Breaking change: false
